faq.q: Why would a tree run out of water in winter?
faq.a: When the soil freezes, its water is locked up as ice that roots cannot absorb. Leaves would keep losing water, so dropping them stops the leak.
asks: Can trees get thirsty in winter?

faq.q: What do trees do before dropping leaves?
faq.a: They break down chlorophyll and move nitrogen and other nutrients from the leaves into the branches and roots. Then a corky layer grows across each leaf stalk so the leaf falls cleanly.
asks: How does a tree let go of its leaves?

faq.q: Why do pine trees keep their needles?
faq.a: Evergreen needles are narrow and coated in thick wax, so they lose little water and shed snow easily. That lets pines keep making food on mild, sunny winter days.

faq.q: How does a tree know when to grow new leaves?
faq.a: Trees respond to longer days and warmer temperatures in spring. Many also need a long enough spell of cold first, so one warm day in midwinter does not fool them.
asks: When do trees grow leaves again?

faq.a: No, they are dormant, a kind of deep rest. Their living cells are protected, and their buds already hold next year's tiny leaves and flowers.

facts: Trees that shed all their leaves each year are called deciduous; those that keep leaves all year are called evergreen.
Next spring's leaves are already formed in miniature inside a tree's winter buds.
In some dry tropical places, trees drop their leaves in the dry season instead of in winter.
